Ex-Chelsea coach Antonio Conte has defended his demanding coaching methods following discussions surrounding his failure to become Manchester United’s manager, insisting that his approach is built on hard work and winning. The Italian tactician said he finds it strange that anyone could be afraid of his methodology, arguing that Manchester United need a strong approach to return to the level of success they enjoyed under former manager Sir Alex Ferguson. Speaking to CronacheTweet on Friday, Conte said, “If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.” Conte also expressed surprise at suggestions that his methods could be a problem for Manchester United, considering the club’s history and ambitions. “Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “They last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson,” he said. Some criticism of Man Utd has crossed the line – CEO NFL legend Tom Brady in talks to buy Chelsea stake – Report EPL: Caicedo, Martinez fit for Chelsea’s Leeds clash The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager revealed that he had read Ferguson’s autobiography and was fortunate to spend time with the legendary Scottish manager at his home in London. “I’ve read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football,” Conte added. The 57-year-old further described some of the comments surrounding his potential appointment at Old Trafford as almost offensive to the club, insisting that a clear methodology is necessary to achieve major success. “That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it’s as if someone were placing a veto on the club’s return to its own history. “A method is what’s needed to achieve major results. And if you’re suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does.
